narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='c1'/>Fifty one squared take away forty nine squared is one hundred. The two add to one hundred.
<bookmark mark='c2'/>Their sum is one hundred, but we must also multiply by their take away, two.
<bookmark mark='c3'/>One hundred times two is two hundred, not one hundred.
removed_beats.on_screen: the hint card leaves; Chintu's bubble shows 51² − 49²; (51 + 49) × (51 − 49) = 100 × 2 = 200 appears; the bubble is struck in the warning colour

narration: <bookmark mark='k1'/>To check, square both numbers and take the smaller from the larger.
<bookmark mark='k2'/>The result must come back to one hundred.
removed_beats.on_screen: the stage clears except the anchor and the answer 100 = 26² − 24²; two check lines appear: square both numbers; take the smaller from the larger

old_misconception.wrong_answer: fifty one squared take away forty nine squared
old_misconception.wrong_move: Chintu picks fifty one and forty nine because they add to one hundred. He forgets to multiply by their take away, two, so he gets two hundred.
